The user wants me to add high‑quality animations to slm_alliance.html, but the file is massive (≈312 KB) and contains several extremely long lines—mostly embedded base64‑encoded font data. Those lines (e.g., line 10, 17, 24, etc.) are each tens of kilobytes long, which makes it impossible to scroll through the file or to understand its structure with a simple “head” or “tail”. 

My earlier attempts confirmed this: a plain `head -100` still produced a huge output, and grepping for “base64” showed the same enormous font lines. I then ran an `awk` that reported the line numbers whose length exceeds 3 000 characters, yielding a list: 10, 17, 24, 378, 383, 388, 393, 398, 403, 408, 413, 418, 423, 428, 433. These are the problematic lines that dominate the file size.

To proceed, I need to look at the actual HTML markup surrounding those lines—especially the parts where I could insert CSS animations or JavaScript. The best approach is to temporarily replace the huge font lines with a short placeholder so the file becomes readable, and then extract a manageable slice of the document that excludes the massive middle block (lines 378‑433) which likely contains more base64 data. 

I’ll use `sed` to substitute lines 10, 17, and 24 with the string “FONTLINE”. Those are the first three huge lines; replacing them will dramatically shrink the top of the file. Next, I’ll pipe the result through `awk` to keep only lines before the start of the middle block (NR ≤ 377) or after its end (NR ≥ 434). This gives me the surrounding HTML without the huge middle section. To avoid dumping the entire file, I’ll cap the output with `head -500` and write it to a temporary file `/tmp/slm_view.txt`. I’ll also check its byte size with `wc -c` so I know how much data I’m dealing with.

Finally, I still need a peek at what’s inside the excluded middle block, because it might contain crucial scripts or style tags. I’ll extract lines 378‑433 directly from the original file, trim each line to the first 200 characters (enough to see the structure without the full base64 payload), and store that in `/tmp/slm_mid.txt`. This two‑pronged extraction will give me a clear, readable view of the HTML layout while still preserving a glimpse of the hidden middle section.

Thus, the next step is to run a Bash command that performs these replacements and extractions exactly as described.

arguments.command: sed -e '10s/.*/FONTLINE/' -e '17s/.*/FONTLINE/' -e '24s/.*/FONTLINE/' /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | awk 'NR<=377 || NR>=434' | head -500 > /tmp/slm_view.txt; wc -c /tmp/slm_view.txt; sed -n '378,433p' /home/lane/MythosMini/slm_alliance.html | cut -c1-200 > /tmp/slm_mid.txt
